name: docs add / edit: entry and feature commands
description: Commands to create and change docs without hand-editing YAML: docs add <feature>[/<entry>] (new feature, or new entry with --kind, --summary, --body, --path/--anchor/--keyword hints), docs edit <feature>[/<entry>] (change summary, body, kind, when hints, feature status), docs rm <feature>[/<entry>]. Validates kinds against config.yaml and entry ids; anchors created from path:line via the anchor model; stamps created/updated through the #25 rules. Same conventions as issues: --json, exit codes, --root, interactive prompts when input is missing, non-interactive mode, git add/mv, lock.
author: cbk <cbk@snappy.no>

comments.author: cbk <cbk@snappy.no>
comments.text: Merged 18bf43d. docs add <feature | feature/entry | repo/entry> (-k, -s, -b/--body-file/--body-stdin, -p/-a/-w hints, --step 'title #n', -e derives the id), docs edit (summary, kind, status, body, add/remove path/anchor/keyword, step edits addressed by their 1-based number from before the edit, --id rename via git mv), docs rm [-f]. Every change is validated, and only problems it introduces are rejected (exit 2). Re-anchor with --add-anchor on the same path:line. JSON: { address, file, feature|entry|repo }. After merging, there is a single strict DocsAddress (Features/Docs) shared with #27. Gaps that would still need YAML hand edits: config.yaml kinds, entry ordering, moving an entry between features.
